name: webxr-service-ui
description: webxr modular UI (Option B). Two entries: View.tsx → ui.js (desktop control panel — react/react-dom/@rlx/ui are host-provided EXTERNALS here, never bundled, same as every other service) and xr/View.tsx → xr.js (immersive in-headset client — `rlx.xrStandalone` below opts this ONE entry out of that: it bundles its own private react+react-dom instead of sharing the host's, because @react-three/fiber vendors its own react-reconciler build and sharing a singleton across that boundary repeatedly broke on React's unstable internals as the host's react-dom patch version and the vendored reconciler drifted apart — see build-service-ui.mjs's `standalone` doc comment). react/react-dom are still pinned under devDependencies (exactly matching botgear_ui's installed version) so npm's peer-dependency resolution — and, for xr.js specifically, the ACTUAL bundled version — line up with what react-reconciler declares it needs, rather than npm free-floating to whatever's newest.
